name: Dropbox
location: Default local file storage: %USERPROFILE%\Dropbox; %USERPROFILE%\Dropbox\.dropbox.cache (up to 3 days of cached data). File storage folder location: SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\SyncRootManager\Dropbox!<SID>!Personal\UserSyncRoots. File metadata and configuration data: %USERPROFILE%\AppData\Local\Dropbox\ (nucleus.sqlite3, sync_history.db, aggregation.dbx = usage and file metadata; older versions: filecache.dbx, config.dbx, both DPAPI-encrypted; info.json = app configuration data).
purpose: Dropbox synchronizes a local folder with the user's cloud account; older client versions encrypt most metadata with Windows DPAPI making it host- and user-bound, while recent versions expose substantially more metadata in plain SQLite databases.
key_fields: nucleus.sqlite3 - current-version usage and file metadata database
SyncRootManager\Dropbox!<SID>!Personal\UserSyncRoots - registry confirmation of the configured sync folder path per user SID
normal_baseline: A single Dropbox account tied to the user's SID under SyncRootManager, local folder activity and nucleus.sqlite3/sync_history.db entries consistent with routine file use, and .dropbox.cache holding only the last few days of transient sync data.
anomalies: sync_history.db or aggregation.dbx showing a large, concentrated batch of uploads shortly before resignation or termination, consistent with data staging for exfiltration (T1567.002)
A Dropbox Personal account configured under SyncRootManager on a corporate-managed endpoint with no business justification
DPAPI-encrypted filecache.dbx/config.dbx present with no way to decrypt outside the original user/host context, potentially masking older activity from investigation
info.json or nucleus.sqlite3 reflecting an account identity inconsistent with the endpoint's assigned user
Evidence of files present in .dropbox.cache with no corresponding entry in nucleus.sqlite3 or sync_history.db, suggesting deletion or tampering with the primary metadata store
parsing_tools: Generic SQLite browser (e.g. DB Browser for SQLite) for nucleus.sqlite3, sync_history.db, aggregation.dbx
DPAPI decryption tooling (requires the original user context/master key) for legacy filecache.dbx and config.dbx
anti_forensic_notes: Older Dropbox client versions encrypt filecache.dbx and config.dbx with Windows DPAPI, which is tied to the user account and host - without that context, this metadata cannot be decrypted, effectively limiting recovery to whatever the newer plaintext databases retain. .dropbox.cache only retains up to three days of cached data, so transient evidence there is short-lived. Consumer Dropbox exposes only a limited "Events" activity page rather than full audit logging, constraining what can be corroborated outside local artifacts.
interpretation: Because encryption scope changed across Dropbox client versions, always identify the installed version before assuming metadata is readable - recent clients (nucleus.sqlite3, sync_history.db, aggregation.dbx) are far more forensically useful than older DPAPI-encrypted ones. Metadata can be recovered for local, cloud, and deleted files alike. Deleted files may exist in both local and online recycle bins; online recycle bin retention is 30 days for Personal accounts and 120 days for Business. Dropbox Business "Advanced" tier provides detailed audit logging, while consumer Dropbox is limited to the basic Events page.
